# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
**40,000 users | Old and new systems run in parallel | Target: production tomorrow**

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system in three phases, using increasing cohort sizes gated by explicit entry criteria. The old system remains fully operational and untouched (no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning) through every phase, including the final migration batch, and is only considered for retirement in a separate, later decommission project.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (2% of users — 800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration tests in staging (invoicing, payment capture, refunds, webhooks, tax calculation) with 100% test suite pass rate, and a rollback procedure has been dry-run successfully at least once.

- Select 800 low-risk internal/opt-in users or users on simple (single-plan, no active disputes) billing profiles.
- Run dual-write/shadow reconciliation: both systems process billing events; outputs are diffed nightly.
- Manual review of every transaction for the first 48 hours.
- Duration: minimum 3 days before proceeding.

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users — 10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completes its minimum duration with zero critical incidents, reconciliation diff rate below 0.1%, and support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.5x of baseline.

- Expand to a representative cross-section of plan types, geographies, and payment methods.
- Automated reconciliation replaces manual per-transaction review; daily summary review only.
- Customer support briefed and on standby with escalation path to engineering.
- Duration: minimum 5 days before proceeding.

## Phase 3: General Availability (73% of users — remaining ~29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completes its minimum duration with all halt-condition metrics (below) remaining under threshold for 5 consecutive days, and finance has signed off on reconciliation accuracy for Phase 2 cohorts.

- Migrate remaining users in daily batches (e.g., 10 batches of ~2,920) rather than a single cutover, to preserve rollback granularity.
- Old billing system remains active in read-only/reconciliation mode for all migrated users through this phase and beyond — it is not deleted, disabled, or decommissioned as part of this or any batch in this phase.
- Final batch is followed by a minimum 14-day parallel-run/observation window on the old system before any separate decommissioning proposal is considered.

---

## Halt / Rollback Metrics

- **Halt the rollout immediately if:** billing reconciliation mismatch rate between old and new systems exceeds **0.5%** of transactions in any rolling 24-hour window.
- Additional guardrails: payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds 2x the pre-migration baseline; support ticket volume for migrated cohort exceeds 3x baseline; any single data-integrity incident (duplicate charge, missed charge) affecting more than 10 users.

---

## Risks

RISK: Double-billing or missed charges due to both systems processing the same invoice | Implement idempotency keys and a single source-of-truth flag per user account; automated nightly reconciliation with alerting | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: New system miscalculates tax or currency conversion for edge-case regions | Run parallel shadow calculations for all migrated users during Phases 1-2 and require finance sign-off before Phase 3 | Finance/Compliance Lead
RISK: Customer support overwhelmed by migration-related tickets during Phase 3 ramp | Pre-stage support scripts, expand on-call rotation, and gate batch size on ticket-volume threshold | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback from new system back to old system fails or loses transactional data | Require a tested, timed rollback runbook per phase and freeze new-system writes during rollback execution | Site Reliability Engineering Lead
RISK: Data migration script corrupts or mismatches customer payment methods | Validate migrated records against source via automated checksum/field-diff before activating new system for each user | Data Migration Lead

PHASES: 3
